questions.stem: A 32-year-old lady is transfused blood prior to a surgical procedure. 15 minutes into the transfusion she complains of difficulty in breathing, itching and rashes over skin. Her speech is slurred, and physician is able to hear strange noise during respiration with bare ears. Pulse is 100/min, feeble, BP is 90/70 and falling. Which of the following constitutes the treatment of choice for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Intramuscular adrenalin. Rashes, slurred speech (? Angioedema), noise during breathing (? Striador due to laryngeal edema) and hypotension are all suggestive of Anaphylactic Shock, adrenalin IM 1;1000 dilution is to be immediately administered in such cases.

questions.stemHtml: In the image slide labelled A is an investigation used in screening for neoplastic/preneoplastic conditions. Which of the following pairs correctly matches?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) In the image A is liquid based cytology which is an advanced technique for interpretation of pap smears and B is conventional pap smear.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a feature of nephrotic syndrome?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Acute renal failure. Acute renal failure results due to decrease in glomerular filtration rate which is seen in acute nephritic not in nephrotic syndromes. If nephritic syndrome progresses to acute renal failure clinically this is known as rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis [RPGN]

questions.stem: An 82-year-old man’s heart weighs less than normal. Which of the following is true?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Heart weighs less is suggestive of atrophy and in old age myocardial atrophy is due to deposition of lipofuscin which gives the cell brown colour thus the name brown atrophy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common type of Hodgkin lymphoma?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Nodular sclerosis is the most common type followed by mixed cellularity. Lymphocyte depleted is the worst prognostic, nodular lymphocyte predominant is the best prognostic.

questions.stemHtml: Histological examination off vessel of a patient who has a long-standing history of hypertension is as follows. Which of the following mechanism is leading to the histological changes seen in this image?

options.label: B
options.text: Plasma protein escape due to endothelial injury

options.label: C
options.text: Fibrin like material due to immune complex damage

questions.answerText: Plasma protein escape due to endothelial injury
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

The image shows hyaline arteriosclerosis which is seen in Benign hypertension. The pink hyaline like material is due to plasma protein escaping from the vessel and compensatory ECM production by the blood vessel.

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is false?

options.label: A

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Hyperemia is due to arteriolar dilation not Venodilation, venous dilation leads to congestion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a part of innate immunity?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) B lymphocytes. Innate immunity consists of inflammatory cells [neutrophils macrophages], compliments, PH of fluids, bodily secretions, NK cell [large granular lymphocyte]. Adaptive immunity consists of humoral [b cell induced] and cell mediated [C8 positive t cells] immunity.

questions.stem: Most important prognostic factor in wilms tumour is?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Histology. Presence of an aplasia on histology is the worst prognostic factor of wilms tumour as they are usually chemo resistant.

questions.stem: Which of the following does not play a role in iron metabolism?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Haptoglobin is a hemoglobin binding protein which prevents renal toxicity of free hemoglobin in the plasma and has no role in iron metabolism.

questions.stem: Severity of the disease increases as the disease passes from one generation to next generation, such a phenomena is seen in?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) All of the above. Increase in severity of the disease with passing generation is known as genetic anticipation which is seen in trinucleotide repeat disorders and all the options given are examples of trinucleotide repeat disorders.

questions.stem: Correct statement regarding immune surveillance.

options.label: A
options.text: Anti CTLA 4 Ab is a new modality in the treatment of early cancers

options.label: B
options.text: Mutation of tumour suppressor genes decreases antigen toxicity

options.label: C
options.text: PD1/PDL1 activation leading to tumour suppression

options.label: D
options.text: Not binding of CD28 leads to immune tolerance.

questions.answerText: Not binding of CD28 leads to immune tolerance.

Anti CTLA-1 (Ipilimumab) and anti PD1 (nivolumab) are used in treatment of many advanced cancers.

questions.stemHtml: A 35-year male presents with cervical lymphadenopathy, biopsy from the lymph node is as shown in the image which of the following is not true regarding this disease?

options.text: Neoplastic cells are CD 20 positive B lymphocytes,

options.label: C
options.text: Spleen involvement is rare in this case

questions.answerText: Neoplastic cells are CD 20 positive B lymphocytes,
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) The image shows classical Reed Sternberg cell making it a diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma. The RS cells are b cells but they are CD 20 negative.

questions.stem: Patient was diagnosed of abdominal aortic aneurysm for which atherosclerosis is suspected to be the most common etiology. Which of the following mechanisms would have led to aneurysm? (1) Destruction of extracellular matrix (2) Ischemic necrosis of cells of the vessel wall (3) Obliterative end-arteritis of vasa vasorum (4) Decreased collagen synthesis
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) 1 and 2 only. Atherosclerosis causes aneurysm by 2 mechanism namely inflammation mediated destruction of vessel wall and decreased blood supply to the inner most smooth muscle in the media [increased thickness of the vessel wall leads to decreased blood supply to the innermost smooth muscle].

questions.stemHtml: A 10-year child presents with bleeding per rectum, colonoscopy shows 2 polyps in the colon and rectum. A polypectomy was done, and the histology is as shown in the image. Which of the following is likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Hamartomatous polyp. The histology shows arborizing smoothe muscle and connective tissue inbetween the glands characteristic of hamartomatous polyp, which is seen in Peutz jaghers syndrome.

questions.stemHtml: Following is the perhaps smear image of a 42-year-old female. what is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) H-SIL. The image shows cells smaller than intermediate cells with hyperchromatic nucleus and very high nucleo cytoplasmic ratio which is characteristic of H- SIL.

questions.stem: A Child has hematuria after a respiratory tract infection, This is 4th episode in the last 8 months. Renal biopsy most likely will show?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Mesangial hypercellularity. Recurrent hematuria after a respiratory tract infection is suggestive of IGA nephropathy which will show mesangial hyperplasia and on long standing can show mesangial sclerosis.

questions.stem: All of the following are markers of seminoma except?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Cytokeratin. Cytokeratin is a marker for embryonal carcinoma and yolk sac tumour. Markers for seminoma include PL AP, CD117, Oct 3/ 4, podoplanin, Nanog.

questions.stem: Which of the following from the dead cells induces inflammation in necrosis but not in apoptosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) DAMP Damage Associated molecular pattern are components released from necrotic cell (due to CM damage) activate TLR and other receptor on neutrophils inducing inflammation. Apoptotic cells are recognised by macrophages due to coating of the apoptotic bodies by Phosphatidyl Serine, thrombospondin & Complements.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors get activated by contact activation? (1) XI (2) XII (3) VII (4) X
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Contact activation [intrinsic pathway] can activate both factor 12 and 11.

options.text: Auto antibodies cross reacting with parietal cells

options.label: C
options.text: Auto antibodies cross reacting with RBC

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

The image shows microcytic hypochromic anemia [suggestive of iron deficiency] and in a patient on long term aspirin which would lead to decrease from TX A2 inducing GI bleed thus chronic blood loss leading to iron deficiency anemia.

questions.stemHtml: A 46-year-old chronic smoker presents with cough, intermittent fever for many weeks. Now he also complains of recent onset of hoarseness of voice, cough. He has lost 6 kg after the onset of the symptoms. On chest X ray showed calcified lung lesion with few hilar lymphadenopathy. Serum calcium levels are increased. A biopsy from the lung is as below what is the likely treatment?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Steroids. The lesion shows discrete noncaseating granulomas suggestive of sarcoidosis. Further hyper calcemia is seen in sarcoidosis (due to increased Vitamin D) is in favour of sarcoid rather than tuberculosis.

questions.stem: Citrate phosphate dextrose is preferred over acid citrate dextrose as a preservative because?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Better O2 delivery. Phosphate increases 2, 3-DPG in the blood which increases the oxygen delivery. Shelf life Blood in both ACD and CPD is 21 days.

questions.stem: Which of the following mechanism off immune system is mediated by IgG?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) IgG can induce cell lysis by all the 3 mechanisms. For complement mediated lysis other immunoglobulins are IgM and IgA. Opsonization is induced by IgG and C3 b, antibody dependent cytotoxicity is mediated by IgG and NK cells.

Correct Answer (B)

A is lined by stratified squamous epithelium which represents etocervix, B is the transformational zone which undergoes metaplasiaà Dysplasiaàcarcinoma. C Represents columnar glands of endocervix and D represents cervical stroma.

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Progresses to squamous cell carcinoma. Barrett's esophagus progresses to adenocarcinoma.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is true about chronic myeloid leukemia?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) In chronic myeloid leukemia the cells are well differentiated into myeloid lineage thus high degree of differentiation and since it is a neoplasm the rate of death has to be less [low apoptosis]

questions.stemHtml: A 12-year child presents with severe pain and swelling in the lower end of the thigh. The pain and swelling has rapidly progressed over last week. options.label: A
options.text: RB mutations are most likely to be seen in this patient

options.label: C
options.text: T(9;22) is seen in this tumor

questions.stemHtml: A 40-year man presents with headache, blurred vision and hand claudication clinical image is as given below. A biopsy from the same is as shows giant cells. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Histology shows giant cells and collagen deposition which is seen both in takayasu and giant cell arteritis. Most important difference between them is age [> 50 is giant cell arteritis, < 50 is takayasu arteritis]

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct order of sequence of progression of lesions of lung adenocarcinoma ? i. Adenocarcinoma ii. Bronchioloalveolar carcinoma iii. Minimally invasive adenocarcinoma iv. Atypical adenomatous hyperplasia
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Iv,ii,iii,i. bronchioloalveolar carcinoma is also called as adenocarcinoma Insitu. The stages of lung adenocarcinoma development is atypical adenomatous hyperplasia (<5mm in overall size)-->Adenocarcinoma insitu (<3 cm no invasion)-->Minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (<5 mm invasion into stroma)--> invasive adenocarcinoma

questions.stem: A 29-year-old lady is being worked up for an elective fistulectomy. She doesn’t have any complains apart from related to fistula. She had 3 abortions in the past. General physical examination is within normal limits. Her coagulation profile shows Prothrombin time of 15 seconds, activated partial thromboplastin time of 56 seconds, platelet count of 188000/cu.mm. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct answer: D - Anti-phospholipid antibodies

Recurrent pregnancy loss with an unexplained prolonged aPTT raises suspicion for antiphospholipid antibodies, particularly a lupus anticoagulant. Such antibodies may prolong phospholipid-dependent clotting tests in vitro despite an association with thrombosis and pregnancy morbidity in vivo. This vignette does not alone establish antiphospholipid syndrome: appropriate antibody testing, persistence and clinical evaluation are required, and other causes of prolonged aPTT must be excluded.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an appropriate step for collection of blood samples?

options.label: A
options.text: The needle should pierce the vein at an angle of 45°

options.label: B
options.text: Tourniquet should be released after withdrawing needle from the patient

options.label: C
options.text: Place a cotton swab at site after collection and ask the patient to fold his arm

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Perform venepuncture as follows. • Anchor the vein by holding the patient’s arm and placing a thumb BELOW the venepuncture site. • Ask the patient to form a fist so the veins are more prominent. • Enter the vein swiftly at a 30 degree angle or less, and continue to introduce the needle along the vein at the easiest angle of entry. • Once sufficient blood has been collected, release the tourniquet BEFORE withdrawing the needle. Some guidelines suggest removing the tourniquet as soon as blood flow is established, and always before it has been in place for two minutes or more. Withdraw the needle gently and apply gentle pressure to the site with a clean gauze or dry cotton-wool ball. Ask the patient to hold the gauze or cotton wool in place, with the arm extended and raised. Ask the patient NOT to bend the arm, because doing so causes a haematoma

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man incurs a stab wound to the chest. The wound is treated in the emergency room. Two months later there is a firm, 3 x 2 cm nodular mass with intact overlying epithelium in the region of the wound. On examination the scar is firm, but not tender, with no erythema. This mass is excised and microscopically shows fibroblasts with abundant haphazardly arranged collagen and no inflammatory cells. Which of the following mechanisms has most likely produced this series of events?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Keloid is excessive collagen deposition with an arrest in proper maturation from Type III to Type I collagen at sites like sternum and ear lobes, the ratio of type I to type III is higher than normal skin. HPE shows haphazardly arranged collagen bundles due to this strength is poor. In hypertrophic scar is limited to the wound area and collagen are type III more than type I but are parallelly arranged here the strength is less due to type III predominance

questions.stem: Most common mutation seen in pancreatic carcinoma is

questions.stem: As an intern you are is studying effects of gene mutation and its phenotypic effects. The phenomenon seen in you study will be called as
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Genetic Pleotrophy. It is a phenomenon in which single mutation leads to multiple phenotypic effects. Genetic heterogeneity is opposite of pleotrophy in which multiple mutation lead to same disease.

questions.stem: Important function of Epithelioid cells in a granuloma
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Epithelioid cells in a granuloma are the principle cells and are activated macrophages, with secretory function. They secrete TNF and IFN to recruit and activate more cells and cause intracellular killing of the offending organism.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old is diagnosed to have an inherited disease due to mutation of HFE gene. Which of the following is not the likely manifestation of this disease?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Type II DM. HFE mutation is seen in primary hemochromatosis which will have type I DM due to destruction of islet cells not type II DM. other manifestation includes malabsorption syndromes, cirrhosis, synovitis.

questions.stem: A child presents with repeated pharyngitis, otitis and pneumonia. Examination shows the lymph nodes are not palpable. Imaging shows absent thymic shadow and a small spleen. Which of the following best fits into the above manifestation?

questions.stem: Most common inherited cause of thrombosis is?
